items.question: Who built the ark?
items.explanation: God told Noah to build an ark to save his family and the animals from the flood.
items.hint: He was a righteous man in his generation.

items.question: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
items.explanation: Jonah ran from God's command and was taken into the fish before being sent to Nineveh.
items.hint: He was sent to the city of Nineveh.

items.question: Who was thrown into the lions' den?
items.explanation: Daniel kept praying to God, so the king had him cast into the den.
items.hint: He served in the court of Babylon.

items.question: Which giant did David defeat with a sling?
items.explanation: David's stone struck the Philistine champion on the forehead.
items.hint: He was a champion from Gath.

items.question: Who was sold into Egypt by his brothers?
items.explanation: His brothers sold him to traders who took him to Egypt.
items.hint: His father gave him a coat of many colours.

items.question: Who led the Israelites out of Egypt?
items.explanation: God sent Moses to bring the people out of slavery.
items.hint: He saw a burning bush.

items.question: Who was the first man?
items.explanation: God formed Adam from the dust of the ground.
items.hint: He lived in the garden of Eden.

items.question: Who was the first woman?
items.explanation: God made Eve from one of Adam's ribs and brought her to him.
items.hint: She was the mother of all the living.

items.question: Which man was swallowed by a fish and then preached in Nineveh?
items.explanation: After his time in the fish, Jonah obeyed God and preached in the great city.
items.hint: His book is short, with four chapters.

items.question: Who was Israel's first king?
items.explanation: Samuel anointed Saul as the first king of Israel.
items.hint: He was taller than the others.

items.question: Who was the shepherd boy who became king?
items.explanation: God chose David, the youngest son of Jesse, to be king.
items.hint: He wrote many psalms.

items.question: Which king was known for great wisdom?
items.explanation: God gave Solomon a wise and understanding heart.
items.hint: He was David's son.

items.question: Who was the mother of Samuel?
items.explanation: Hannah prayed for a child, and God answered her.
items.hint: She dedicated her son to the Lord at Shiloh.

items.question: Who was the wife of Abraham?
items.explanation: God changed her name and promised she would be the mother of nations.
items.hint: Her name was once Sarai.

items.question: Whose wife looked back and became a pillar of salt?
items.explanation: Lot's wife disobeyed God's warning when Sodom was destroyed.
items.hint: She was leaving the city with her family.

items.question: Which wall fell after the people marched around it?
items.explanation: The walls fell down flat when the people shouted at God's command.
items.hint: Joshua led the army to this city.

items.question: Who was the first murderer in the Bible?
items.explanation: Cain killed his brother Abel out of jealousy.
items.hint: He was a farmer.

items.question: Who was the strongest man in the Old Testament?
items.explanation: God gave Samson great strength, which he used for Israel's deliverance.
items.hint: His hair was never cut.

items.question: Who wrestled with an angel by the river Jabbok?
items.explanation: Jacob held on until he received a blessing, and his name was changed to Israel.
items.hint: He was the son of Isaac.

items.question: Which book is named after a woman from Moab who was loyal to Naomi?
items.explanation: Ruth stayed with Naomi and worshipped the Lord.
items.hint: She gleaned in the fields of Boaz.

items.question: Who was the queen who saved the Jews in Persia?
items.explanation: Esther risked her life to speak to the king for her people.
items.hint: Her cousin was Mordecai.

items.question: How many days did it rain during the flood?
items.explanation: The rain fell for forty days and forty nights.
items.hint: The number forty appears often in the Bible.

items.question: What did God set in the sky as a sign of his promise after the flood?
items.explanation: The rainbow is a sign of the covenant with Noah.
items.hint: It appears after rain.

items.question: Which mountain did Noah's ark rest on?
items.explanation: The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
items.hint: It is in the region of modern Turkey.

items.question: Which tree did Adam and Eve eat from against God's command?
items.answer: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
options: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
items.explanation: God forbade them to eat from it.
items.hint: It was in the middle of the garden.

items.question: Who was the father of the twelve tribes of Israel?
items.explanation: Jacob's twelve sons became the heads of the tribes.
items.hint: God renamed him Israel.

items.question: Who was the brother of Moses who spoke for him?
items.explanation: Aaron spoke to Pharaoh on behalf of Moses.
items.hint: He became the first high priest.

items.question: Which sea did God divide to let Israel escape Egypt?
items.explanation: The waters stood as a wall on each side of the people.
items.hint: Egyptian chariots followed them.

items.question: What food did God send from heaven in the wilderness?
items.explanation: Each morning the people gathered manna to eat.
items.hint: The name means 'What is it?'.

items.question: What did God give Moses on Mount Sinai?
items.explanation: God spoke the commandments and wrote them on stone tablets.
items.hint: They begin with 'I am the LORD thy God'.

items.question: Who was Rahab's city?
items.explanation: Rahab hid the two spies in her house on the city wall.
items.hint: Her house was built into the wall.

items.question: Who hid two spies on the roof under stalks of flax?
items.explanation: Rahab hid the spies and helped them escape.
items.hint: She lived in Jericho.

items.question: Which judge led an army of three hundred men?
items.explanation: God reduced the army so that Israel would know the victory came from him.
items.hint: He once asked God for a sign with a fleece.

items.question: Who was the woman who judged Israel under a palm tree?
items.explanation: Deborah judged Israel and encouraged Barak to fight.
items.hint: She was also a prophetess.

items.question: Who was the prophet who anointed Saul?
items.explanation: Samuel poured oil on Saul's head to show that God had chosen him.
items.hint: He was raised by Eli at Shiloh.

items.question: Who was the prophet who called fire down on Mount Carmel?
items.explanation: God answered Elijah's prayer and the fire consumed the sacrifice.
items.hint: He opposed the prophets of Baal.

items.question: Who was Elijah's successor as prophet?
items.explanation: Elisha received a double portion of Elijah's spirit.
items.hint: He saw Elijah taken up in a whirlwind.

items.question: Which prophet was taken to heaven in a whirlwind?
items.explanation: A chariot of fire separated Elijah from Elisha and he went up in the whirlwind.
items.hint: He was the prophet of Mount Carmel.

items.question: Which king of Babylon saw a statue with feet of iron and clay?
items.explanation: Daniel explained the dream of the great statue.
items.hint: He ruled Babylon.

items.question: Who wrote most of the Psalms?
items.explanation: Many psalms are attributed to David, the shepherd king.
items.hint: He is called the sweet psalmist of Israel.

items.question: Which Old Testament book is a collection of wise sayings?
items.explanation: Proverbs teaches wisdom for daily life.
items.hint: Solomon is named as its author.

items.question: Which book has the sentence 'Vanity of vanities; all is vanity'?
items.explanation: The Preacher reflects on the meaning of life 'under the sun'.
items.hint: It is a short book in the wisdom books.

items.question: Who was the man of great patience who lost his children and wealth?
items.explanation: Job kept faith in God through severe trials.
items.hint: He lived in the land of Uz.

items.question: Which prophet was called in his youth: 'Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child'?
items.explanation: God called Jeremiah as a prophet to the nations.
items.hint: He is called the weeping prophet.

items.question: Who was the king who received a long life extension of fifteen years?
items.explanation: God answered Hezekiah's prayer after he was sick.
items.hint: The sun went backward as a sign.

items.question: Which king repaired the temple and found the book of the law?
items.explanation: Hilkiah found the book in the temple and it was read to the king.
items.hint: He was a boy king.

items.question: Who received the words 'Be fruitful, and multiply' in the garden?
items.explanation: God blessed the first humans and gave them this command.
items.hint: It happened on the sixth day of creation.

items.question: How many days did God take to create the world?
items.explanation: God created the world in six days and rested on the seventh.
items.hint: Look at the account at the start of Genesis.

items.question: On which day did God rest?
items.explanation: God finished his work and rested from it.
items.hint: It is the sabbath.

items.question: What did God create on the first day?
items.explanation: God said, 'Let there be light', and there was light.
items.hint: The sun was made on the fourth day.

items.question: Which brother was murdered by Cain?
items.explanation: Abel offered a sacrifice that God accepted, and Cain killed him in anger.
items.hint: He was a shepherd.

items.question: Who was the father of Isaac?
items.explanation: God gave Abraham and Sarah a son in their old age.
items.hint: He left Ur at God's call.

items.question: Who did Abraham almost sacrifice on Mount Moriah?
items.explanation: God tested Abraham's faith and provided a ram instead.
items.hint: He was the son of the promise.

items.question: Which son of Isaac sold his birthright for a bowl of stew?
items.explanation: Esau gave up his birthright to his brother for food.
items.hint: He was a skilful hunter.

items.question: Who was the mother of Joseph?
items.explanation: God remembered Rachel and she bore Joseph.
items.hint: She died giving birth to Benjamin.

items.question: Who was the father of Jesse?
items.explanation: Obed was the son of Ruth and Boaz and the grandfather of David.
items.hint: Ruth was his mother.

items.question: Who was the wife of Boaz?
items.explanation: Ruth became the wife of Boaz and the great-grandmother of David.
items.hint: She was a Moabite.

items.question: Which mountain did God speak to Moses from?
items.explanation: God came down on Mount Sinai and gave the law.
items.hint: It is also called Horeb in some places.

items.question: Which tabernacle furniture held the Ten Commandments?
items.explanation: The tablets of stone were placed inside the ark.
items.hint: It was covered with a mercy seat.

items.question: What did Moses use to strike the rock for water?
items.explanation: God told Moses to strike the rock at Horeb so water would come out.
items.hint: The rod was used before in signs in Egypt.

items.question: Which animal spoke to Balaam?
items.explanation: God opened the mouth of the donkey to rebuke Balaam.
items.hint: Balaam was riding it.

items.question: Who was the high priest in Eli's time?
items.explanation: Eli sat by the doorpost of the temple at Shiloh.
items.hint: He trained the boy Samuel.

items.question: Who killed the giant Goliath?
items.explanation: With a stone from his sling, David defeated the Philistine.
items.hint: He was a young shepherd.

items.question: Who was David's best friend?
items.explanation: Jonathan loved David as his own soul and made a covenant with him.
items.hint: He was the son of Saul.

items.question: Who was the son of David who was known for his beautiful hair?
items.explanation: Absalom rebelled against his father and was killed.
items.hint: His hair was heavy when he cut it.

items.question: Who was the prophet who told David 'Thou art the man'?
items.explanation: Nathan confronted David with his sin involving Bathsheba.
items.hint: He also helped Solomon become king.

items.question: Who built the temple in Jerusalem?
items.explanation: Solomon completed the temple in the fourth year of his reign.
items.hint: His father had wanted to build it.

items.question: Who was Solomon's mother?
items.explanation: Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah and then of David.
items.hint: She had a son named Solomon.

items.question: Who was Solomon's father?
items.explanation: David declared that Solomon would reign after him.
items.hint: He was the king of Judah and Israel.

items.question: Which queen visited Solomon to test his wisdom?
items.explanation: She came with riddles and was amazed at his wisdom.
items.hint: She travelled a long way from the south.

items.question: Which prophet confronted King Ahab and Jezebel about Naboth's vineyard?
items.explanation: Elijah announced judgement for the murder of Naboth.
items.hint: He was a prophet from Tishbe.

items.question: Who was the wicked queen who had many prophets of the Lord killed?
items.explanation: Jezebel promoted the worship of Baal and opposed God's prophets.
items.hint: She was married to Ahab.

items.question: Who was the woman in Shunem who gave a room to Elisha?
items.explanation: She provided a room for the prophet and God gave her a son.
items.hint: Her husband was old.

items.question: Who cured Naaman's leprosy by washing in the Jordan River?
items.explanation: Elisha told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan.
items.hint: Naaman was a commander of the Syrian army.

items.question: Who was the servant of Elisha who took money from Naaman?
items.explanation: Gehazi lied to Naaman and was struck with leprosy.
items.hint: He was Elisha's servant.

items.question: Which king of Judah was struck with leprosy for offering incense in the temple?
items.explanation: Uzziah became proud and entered the temple to burn incense.
items.hint: He is also called Azariah.

items.question: Who led the people back from Babylon to rebuild the temple?
items.explanation: Zerubbabel led the return and the building of the second temple.
items.hint: He was a governor of Judah.

items.question: Who read the law to the people after the return from exile?
items.explanation: Ezra read the book of the law from morning until midday.
items.hint: He was a priest and scribe.

items.question: Who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem?
items.explanation: Nehemiah organised the people to rebuild the walls in fifty-two days.
items.hint: He was cupbearer to the king of Persia.

items.question: Who was the high priest who saw Samuel's call?
items.explanation: Eli helped Samuel understand that God was calling him.
items.hint: He was a priest at Shiloh.

items.question: What was the name of Moses' mother?
items.explanation: She was the mother of Aaron and Moses.
items.hint: Her name is listed in the genealogy of Levi.

items.question: Who was the sister of Moses who watched over him in the river?
items.explanation: Miriam watched the basket among the reeds.
items.hint: She later sang after the Red Sea crossing.

items.question: Which judge was a woman who killed Sisera with a tent peg?
items.explanation: Jael drove a tent peg through Sisera's head.
items.hint: She was the wife of Heber.

items.question: Which man asked God for a fleece to test his call?
items.explanation: Gideon placed wool on the threshing floor to test God's promise.
items.hint: He was threshing wheat in a winepress.

items.question: Who was the father of Samson?
items.explanation: An angel announced Samson's birth to Manoah's wife.
items.hint: He prayed that the angel would return.

items.question: Who did Samson love and who betrayed him?
items.explanation: Delilah learned the secret of Samson's strength and told the Philistines.
items.hint: She lived in the valley of Sorek.

items.question: Which prophet said 'Here am I; send me'?
items.explanation: After seeing the Lord high and lifted up, Isaiah responded to God's call.
items.hint: His vision took place in the temple.

items.question: Which prophet saw a vision of a valley of dry bones?
items.explanation: God asked Ezekiel whether the bones could live and then breathed life into them.
items.hint: He was a priest taken to Babylon.

items.question: Who was the prophet whose marriage pictured Israel's unfaithfulness?
items.explanation: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, pictured as Israel's faithlessness.
items.hint: His name means 'salvation'.

items.question: Which prophet was a shepherd from Tekoa?
items.explanation: Amos was a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs who prophesied to Israel.
items.hint: He lived in the time of Uzziah and Jeroboam.

items.question: Which prophet was from Moresheth and spoke about Bethlehem's ruler?
items.explanation: Micah prophesied that a ruler would come from Bethlehem.
items.hint: He is one of the minor prophets.

items.question: Which prophet describes the 'day of the LORD' as darkness?
items.explanation: Joel warned that the day of the Lord is a day of darkness and gloominess.
items.hint: A plague of locusts is central to his book.

items.question: Which prophet was sent to Nineveh and ran away to Tarshish?
items.explanation: Jonah boarded a ship to flee from the presence of the Lord.
items.hint: He prayed inside the fish.

items.question: Which prophet wrote about the city of Nineveh falling?
items.explanation: Nahum announced the destruction of Nineveh.
items.hint: His prophecy is short and fierce.

items.question: Which prophet asked 'How long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear?'
items.explanation: Habakkuk questioned God about injustice in Judah.
items.hint: He wrote a prayer that ends with joy in the Lord.

items.question: Which prophet says 'The just shall live by his faith'?
items.explanation: This verse is quoted by Paul in the New Testament.
items.hint: It appears near the end of his second chapter.

items.question: Which prophet told the people to build the house of God?
items.explanation: Haggai urged the people to rebuild the temple.
items.hint: His prophecy is very short.

items.question: Which prophet saw a vision of a man riding a red horse among myrtle trees?
items.explanation: The vision shows God's concern for Jerusalem.
items.hint: He prophesied with Haggai.

items.question: Which prophet calls God's people to return and asks, 'Will a man rob God?'
items.explanation: Malachi rebukes the people for withholding tithes.
items.hint: He is the last book of the Old Testament.

items.question: Which prophet said, 'Behold, I send my messenger before my face'?
items.explanation: This verse points forward to the coming of the Lord and his messenger.
items.hint: It is in the final chapters of the Old Testament.

items.question: Which prophet was a young man called to prophesy against the people of Anathoth?
items.explanation: Jeremiah was from the priests of Anathoth.
items.hint: He was called during the time of Josiah.

items.question: Which prophet declared that the new covenant would be written on hearts?
items.explanation: God promised to write his law on the hearts of his people.
items.hint: He lived before the fall of Jerusalem.

items.question: Who prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem and wept over it?
items.explanation: Jeremiah lamented the state of Judah.
items.hint: He is called the weeping prophet.

items.question: Which book contains the lament: 'How doth the city sit solitary'?
items.explanation: This book mourns the fall of Jerusalem.
items.hint: It is placed after Jeremiah.

items.question: Which book is a love poem between a bride and bridegroom?
items.explanation: This book celebrates love in marriage.
items.hint: It is attributed to Solomon.

items.question: Which prophet was told to eat a scroll that tasted sweet?
items.explanation: God gave Ezekiel the word to speak to Israel.
items.hint: The scroll was as sweet as honey.

items.question: Which king of Israel built a high place for Asherah and was rebuked by Elijah?
items.explanation: Ahab did evil in the sight of the Lord and worshipped Baal.
items.hint: He married Jezebel.

items.question: Which king of Judah was known for reforming the worship in the temple?
items.explanation: Hezekiah opened the doors of the temple and cleansed it.
items.hint: He is also known for the Siloam tunnel.

items.question: Which king prayed that God would heal him, and was given fifteen more years?
items.explanation: God heard the king's prayer and added fifteen years to his life.
items.hint: Isaiah brought the message.

items.question: Which king sent a letter to Hezekiah mocking the God of Israel?
items.explanation: The king of Assyria sent a letter threatening Jerusalem.
items.hint: The Assyrians besieged the city.

items.question: Who was the prophet who advised Hezekiah about the Assyrian threat?
items.explanation: Isaiah sent a message from God that Jerusalem would be delivered.
items.hint: He was a prophet in Jerusalem.

items.question: How many men died in one night when the angel of the Lord struck the Assyrian camp?
items.explanation: The angel of the Lord struck down the Assyrian army in one night.
items.hint: The number is given in the account of Hezekiah.

items.question: Who led the army against Jericho after Moses died?
items.explanation: God commanded Joshua to lead the people across the Jordan.
items.hint: He was Moses' assistant.

items.question: Which spies brought back a good report of the land along with Joshua?
items.explanation: Caleb said the people should go up and possess the land.
items.hint: He later received Hebron as an inheritance.

items.question: Which bird did God send to feed Elijah beside the brook Cherith?
items.explanation: God commanded ravens to bring bread and meat to Elijah.
items.hint: The brook is east of the Jordan.

items.question: Who was the widow of Zarephath who fed Elijah?
items.explanation: The widow shared her last meal with the prophet and God kept her jar of meal full.
items.hint: She lived in Sidon.

items.question: Which prophet was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven?
items.explanation: Elijah was taken up while Elisha watched.
items.hint: A chariot of fire appeared.

items.question: Which king of Israel was known for turning to the Lord with all his heart after Moses' law?
items.explanation: No king before or after him turned to the Lord as he did.
items.hint: He reformed worship in the land.

items.question: Which king of Israel was rebuked by the prophet Ahijah for splitting the nation?
items.explanation: Ahijah tore his garment and told Jeroboam he would rule ten tribes.
items.hint: He set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

items.question: Who was the son of Solomon who lost the ten tribes?
items.explanation: Rehoboam refused the request of the people and most of the tribes rebelled.
items.hint: He listened to his young advisers.

items.question: What were the names of the two golden calves set up by Jeroboam?
items.explanation: Jeroboam set up calves at Bethel and Dan to keep the people from Jerusalem.
items.hint: Both towns are in the north.

items.question: Which man saw the Lord sitting on a throne high and lifted up in the temple?
items.explanation: Isaiah saw the glory of the Lord in a vision.
items.hint: The seraphim cried 'Holy, holy, holy'.

items.question: What were the Hebrew names of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
items.explanation: Their Babylonian names were given by the king's officer.
items.hint: Daniel's Hebrew name was Daniel too.

items.question: Who was thrown into a fiery furnace and not harmed?
items.explanation: God protected the three friends in the furnace.
items.hint: A fourth figure was seen with them.

items.question: Which Babylonian king saw the writing on the wall?
items.explanation: A hand wrote on the plaster of the palace wall at a feast.
items.hint: Daniel interpreted the writing.

items.question: Which words did Daniel read on the wall: 'MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN'?
items.explanation: Daniel explained that the kingdom had been weighed and found wanting.
items.hint: The words describe the kingdom's end.

items.question: Which king of Persia allowed the Jews to return to Jerusalem?
items.explanation: Cyrus made a decree that the temple should be rebuilt.
items.hint: He is called God's anointed in Isaiah.

items.question: Which Persian king made Esther his queen?
items.explanation: Xerxes, also called Ahasuerus, chose Esther after Vashti was removed.
items.hint: Vashti refused to come when called.

items.question: Who was Mordecai's cousin who was raised by him?
items.explanation: Esther was an orphan and Mordecai raised her as his own daughter.
items.hint: She was of the tribe of Benjamin.

items.question: What feast was established to remember the deliverance of the Jews in Esther's time?
items.explanation: The feast of Purim was celebrated as a memorial of the deliverance.
items.hint: Lots were cast before Haman.

items.question: Which wicked official plotted to destroy the Jews in Persia?
items.explanation: Haman was angry that Mordecai would not bow down to him.
items.hint: He was hanged on the gallows he had built.

items.question: Which prophet was sent to speak to Eli's family about their disobedience?
items.explanation: An unnamed man of God pronounced judgement on Eli's house.
items.hint: The Bible does not give his name here.

items.question: Which priest's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were wicked?
items.explanation: Eli's sons did not know the Lord and abused the offerings.
items.hint: They died in battle.

items.question: What was the name of the ark's temporary home in the Philistine city of Ashdod?
items.explanation: The Philistines placed the ark beside their god Dagon, which fell down.
items.hint: Dagon was a Philistine god.

items.question: Who was the first king of the northern kingdom after the division?
items.explanation: Jeroboam was made king over Israel after the ten tribes rebelled.
items.hint: He set up golden calves.

items.question: Which judge sacrificed his daughter because of a vow?
items.explanation: Jephthah made a vow before battle and his daughter came out to meet him.
items.hint: He was a Gileadite.

items.question: Who was the Edomite king who was not an Israelite but ruled before Israel had a king?
items.explanation: Genesis lists the kings of Edom before Israel had a king.
items.hint: He was the son of Beor.

items.question: Which king of Moab was defeated by Ehud?
items.explanation: Ehud killed Eglon with a dagger in his private chamber.
items.hint: He was left-handed.

items.question: Which king of Bashan had a bed of iron?
items.explanation: Og was a giant king of Bashan who was defeated by Israel.
items.hint: His bed was nine cubits long.

items.question: Which king of the Amorites refused Israel passage through his land?
items.explanation: Sihon gathered his army and fought against Israel.
items.hint: Israel took his land east of the Jordan.

items.question: Who was the Moabite king who hired Balaam to curse Israel?
items.explanation: Balak sent messengers to Balaam to curse the people.
items.hint: He was afraid of Israel's numbers.

items.question: What was the name of the man from Midian who married a Moabite woman and was killed by Phinehas?
items.explanation: Zimri brought a Midianite woman into the camp in public.
items.hint: Phinehas stopped the plague by his zeal.

items.question: Which man was Moses' father-in-law who advised him to appoint judges?
items.explanation: Jethro suggested sharing the burden of judging the people.
items.hint: He was a priest of Midian.

items.question: Who was Moses' wife who was a Midianite?
items.explanation: Zipporah was the daughter of Reuel, a priest of Midian.
items.hint: She circumcised their son.

items.question: Which prophet raised the son of the Shunammite woman from the dead?
items.explanation: Elisha lay on the child and his flesh became warm.
items.hint: He was the servant of Elijah.

items.question: Which prophet was known as the 'man of God' who prophesied to Jeroboam at Bethel?
items.answer: A man of God from Judah
options: A man of God from Judah
items.explanation: The prophet from Judah spoke against the altar at Bethel.
items.hint: The Bible describes him as coming from Judah.

items.question: Which king had a wife named Athaliah who killed the royal family?
items.explanation: Athaliah destroyed the royal family, but Joash was hidden in the temple.
items.hint: She was the daughter of Ahab.

items.question: Which priest hid the young king Joash in the temple?
items.explanation: Jehoiada rescued Joash and later helped him become king.
items.hint: He was the high priest.

items.question: Which prophet told King Asa he would be strong if he trusted God?
items.explanation: Azariah reminded Asa that the Lord is with those who are with him.
items.hint: Asa had won against a great army.

items.question: Who was the Moabite woman who said 'Whither thou goest, I will go'?
items.explanation: Ruth committed herself to Naomi and her people.
items.hint: Orpah returned to her family.

items.question: Which man sat under a tree while God revealed he would be the deliverer of Israel?
items.explanation: The angel of the Lord sat under an oak tree in Ophrah.
items.hint: He was threshing wheat in a winepress.

items.question: Which warrior judge was helped by Deborah?
items.explanation: Barak agreed to fight only if Deborah went with him.
items.hint: He was from Naphtali.

items.question: Which woman was given a son after her prayers, and then sang a song of thanksgiving?
items.explanation: Hannah praised God for his salvation and for lifting up the poor.
items.hint: Her son was Samuel.

items.question: Who said 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth'?
items.explanation: The boy Samuel answered God's call in the temple.
items.hint: He grew up in the house of Eli.

items.question: Who was the commander of David's army who killed Uriah?
items.explanation: Joab arranged for Uriah to be placed in danger in battle.
items.hint: He was David's nephew.

items.question: Which man was David's son who killed Amnon?
items.explanation: Absalom had Amnon killed after the attack on Tamar.
items.hint: He later rebelled against David.

items.question: Which king had a counsellor named Ahithophel who joined Absalom's rebellion?
items.explanation: Ahithophel supported Absalom against his former king.
items.hint: The king fled Jerusalem.

items.question: Who cursed David as he fled from Absalom?
items.explanation: Shimei threw stones and cursed the king on the road.
items.hint: He was from the family of Saul.

items.question: Which captain of David's army was Absalom's cousin and fought against him?
items.explanation: Joab killed Absalom when his hair caught in an oak tree.
items.hint: He was the commander of the army.

items.question: Who was the mother of Jesus?
items.explanation: The angel Gabriel told Mary she would conceive and bear a son.
items.hint: She lived in Nazareth.

items.question: Who was the cousin of Jesus who baptised him?
items.explanation: John baptised Jesus in the Jordan River.
items.hint: He wore clothing of camel's hair.

items.question: In which town was Jesus born?
items.explanation: Joseph and Mary travelled to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born.
items.hint: It is also called the city of David.

items.question: Where did Jesus grow up?
items.explanation: After the visit to Jerusalem, the family returned to their own city.
items.hint: It is in Galilee.

items.question: Which disciple was a tax collector?
items.explanation: Jesus called Matthew from his tax booth to follow him.
items.hint: He also wrote the first Gospel.

items.question: Which disciple was also called Didymus?
items.explanation: Didymus means 'twin' in Greek.
items.hint: He wanted to see the nail marks.

items.question: Who was the brother of Peter?
items.explanation: Andrew brought Peter to Jesus.
items.hint: He was a fisherman with his brother.

items.question: Which two brothers were called 'Sons of Thunder'?
items.explanation: Jesus gave them this name, perhaps for their temper.
items.hint: They were fishermen by the Sea of Galilee.

items.question: How many disciples did Jesus choose as apostles?
items.explanation: Jesus chose twelve from among his disciples to be apostles.
items.hint: The number matches the tribes of Israel.

items.question: Who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver?
items.explanation: Judas agreed to hand Jesus over to the chief priests.
items.hint: He carried the money bag.

items.question: Who denied Jesus three times before the cock crew?
items.explanation: Peter denied knowing Jesus, as Jesus had foretold.
items.hint: He wept bitterly afterwards.

items.question: Which garden did Jesus pray in before his arrest?
items.explanation: Jesus prayed there while the disciples slept.
items.hint: It is at the foot of the Mount of Olives.

items.question: What did Jesus turn water into at the wedding in Cana?
items.explanation: This was Jesus' first sign, which showed his glory.
items.hint: The steward tasted it and was surprised.

items.question: How many loaves and fish did Jesus use to feed the five thousand?
options: Seven loaves and a few fish
items.explanation: A boy's meal was blessed and shared by Jesus.
items.hint: Twelve baskets of pieces were left over.

items.question: On which sea did Jesus walk on the water?
items.explanation: The disciples were frightened when they saw him walking towards them.
items.hint: It is also called Lake Gennesaret.

items.question: Who was the disciple who walked on water toward Jesus until he doubted?
items.explanation: Peter began to sink when he looked at the wind.
items.hint: Jesus caught him and lifted him up.

items.question: Which parable tells of a man robbed on the road to Jericho?
items.explanation: The Samaritan showed mercy when others passed by.
items.hint: Jesus told it in answer to 'Who is my neighbour?'

items.question: Which parable tells of a son who left home and came back?
items.explanation: The father welcomed his son home with joy.
items.hint: It is in the chapter about lost things.

items.question: Which parable compares the kingdom to a tiny seed that grows large?
items.explanation: The small seed becomes a tree where birds can rest.
items.hint: It is one of the parables of the kingdom.

items.question: Who did Jesus say was 'the good shepherd'?
items.explanation: Jesus said he was the good shepherd who gives his life for the sheep.
items.hint: The sheep know his voice.

items.question: What is the shortest verse in the Bible?
items.explanation: Jesus wept at the grave of Lazarus.
items.hint: It is in the Gospel of John.

items.question: What did Jesus raise from the dead in Bethany?
items.explanation: Jesus called Lazarus out of the tomb after four days.
items.hint: Lazarus was a friend of Jesus.

items.question: Which sisters lived in Bethany with Lazarus?
items.explanation: Jesus loved this family.
items.hint: One sister was busy serving while the other sat at Jesus' feet.

items.question: Who was the tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus?
items.explanation: He was short and climbed a sycamore tree.
items.hint: Jesus invited himself to his house.

items.question: Who was the blind man healed outside Jericho who called out to Jesus?
items.explanation: The blind beggar cried out to the son of David and received his sight.
items.hint: His name means 'son of Timaeus'.

items.question: Who was the man healed at the pool of Bethesda?
items.answer: A man who had been sick for thirty-eight years
options: A man who had been sick for thirty-eight years
A man with a withered hand
items.explanation: Jesus told him to take up his bed and walk.
items.hint: The pool had five porches.

items.question: What did Jesus say to the paralysed man his friends lowered through a roof?
items.explanation: Jesus forgave the man's sins and then healed him.
items.hint: The roof was opened to let him in.

items.question: Who was the woman who touched Jesus' garment and was healed?
items.answer: A woman with an issue of blood
options: A woman with an issue of blood
items.explanation: She had suffered for twelve years and was made whole by her faith.
items.hint: Jesus felt power go out of him.

items.question: Which Jewish ruler came to Jesus at night?
items.explanation: He came to Jesus and learned about being born again.
items.hint: He later helped bury Jesus.

items.question: Who said 'Behold the Lamb of God'?
items.explanation: John pointed to Jesus as the one who takes away the sin of the world.
items.hint: He was in the wilderness of Judea.

items.question: What was Jesus' first miracle recorded in John?
items.explanation: This sign at Cana showed his glory.
items.hint: The guests were at a wedding.

items.question: Who was the Pharisee who asked Jesus about the greatest commandment?
items.explanation: The lawyer tested Jesus by asking about the law.
items.hint: Jesus answered by quoting Deuteronomy.

items.question: What is the greatest commandment according to Jesus?
items.answer: Love the Lord thy God with all thy heart
options: Love the Lord thy God with all thy heart
items.explanation: Jesus said the first commandment is to love God wholly.
items.hint: The second is like it: love your neighbour.

items.question: Who was the centurion whose servant Jesus healed without going to his house?
items.explanation: The centurion believed that Jesus could heal by a word.
items.hint: Jesus marvelled at his faith.

items.question: Who asked Jesus, 'Who is my neighbour?'
items.explanation: This question led to the parable of the Good Samaritan.
items.hint: He wanted to justify himself.

items.question: Who was the widow of Nain whose son Jesus raised?
items.explanation: Jesus had compassion on the widow and raised her son.
items.hint: The town is in Galilee.

items.question: What did the prodigal son eat with the pigs?
items.explanation: He was hungry in a far country and wished to eat the husks.
items.hint: He came to himself and returned home.

items.question: What is the name of the place where Jesus was crucified?
items.explanation: The name means 'place of a skull'.
items.hint: It was outside Jerusalem.

items.question: Who carried the cross for Jesus?
items.explanation: A passer-by was made to carry the cross.
items.hint: He came from North Africa.

items.question: What was written above Jesus' head on the cross?
items.explanation: Pilate had the words written in three languages.
items.hint: It was written in Hebrew, Greek and Latin.

items.question: Who buried Jesus in his own new tomb?
items.explanation: Joseph asked Pilate for the body and laid it in his tomb.
items.hint: He was a rich man and a disciple.

items.question: Who were the first to see the empty tomb?
items.explanation: The women came at dawn and found the stone rolled away.
items.hint: An angel spoke to them.

items.question: Which two disciples walked to Emmaus and met the risen Jesus?
items.explanation: They did not recognise Jesus until he broke bread with them.
items.hint: They were going to a village near Jerusalem.

items.question: What did Jesus ask Peter three times?
options: Who do you say I am?
items.explanation: Jesus restored Peter after his three denials.
items.hint: He told Peter to feed his sheep.

items.question: On which feast day did the Holy Spirit come upon the disciples?
items.explanation: The disciples were gathered together when the Spirit came like a mighty wind.
items.hint: It is fifty days after Passover.

items.question: Who was the first martyr of the Christian church?
items.explanation: Stephen was stoned for preaching Jesus, and he prayed for his killers.
items.hint: He was one of the seven deacons.

items.question: Who was struck blind on the road to Damascus?
items.explanation: Saul saw a light from heaven and heard the voice of Jesus.
items.hint: He was later known as Paul.

items.question: Who was the man in Damascus who laid hands on Saul?
items.explanation: Ananias obeyed God and restored Saul's sight.
items.hint: He was a disciple living in Damascus.

items.question: Who was the Ethiopian official baptised by Philip?
items.answer: The eunuch of the Ethiopian queen
options: The eunuch of the Ethiopian queen
items.explanation: Philip explained Isaiah 53 and baptised him on the road to Gaza.
items.hint: He was reading the book of Isaiah in his chariot.

items.question: Who was the woman in Joppa raised from the dead by Peter?
items.explanation: Peter prayed and told her to arise.
items.hint: She made clothes for the poor.

items.question: Which seller of purple cloth became a believer in Philippi?
items.explanation: The Lord opened her heart to heed Paul's words.
items.hint: She was from Thyatira.

items.question: Who were the tentmakers Paul worked with in Corinth?
items.explanation: They were Jews expelled from Rome who welcomed Paul.
items.hint: Paul worked with them as a tentmaker.

items.question: Who was Paul's companion on his first missionary journey?
items.explanation: The Holy Spirit called Barnabas and Saul to the work.
items.hint: He was from Cyprus.

items.question: Who was the young man who fell asleep during Paul's sermon and fell from a window?
items.explanation: Paul raised him back to life.
items.hint: The meeting was in Troas.

items.question: Which apostle was shipwrecked on the island of Malta?
items.explanation: Paul was bitten by a viper and was not harmed.
items.hint: He was on his way to Rome as a prisoner.

items.question: Which letter did Paul write to the Christians in Rome?
items.explanation: Paul writes about justification by faith.
items.hint: It is the first long letter after Acts.

items.question: Which book describes the seven churches of Asia?
items.explanation: John writes letters to the seven churches.
items.hint: It ends the Bible.

items.question: Which apostle wrote the most letters in the New Testament?
items.explanation: Paul's letters make up a large part of the New Testament.
items.hint: He was once a persecutor of the church.

items.question: Who is called the beloved physician in the Bible?
items.explanation: Paul mentions Luke as the beloved physician.
items.hint: He wrote the Gospel and the book of Acts.

items.question: Which faithful disciple was Paul's young son in the faith?
items.explanation: Paul called Timothy his true son in the faith.
items.hint: His mother and grandmother were believers.

items.question: To whom did Paul write a letter about a runaway slave named Onesimus?
items.explanation: Paul asked Philemon to receive Onesimus as a brother.
items.hint: It is the shortest letter by Paul.

items.question: Which book is the last in the Bible?
items.explanation: The book ends with a blessing on the saints.
items.hint: It is a book of visions.

items.question: Which letter of John begins 'That which was from the beginning'?
items.explanation: John writes about the word of life.
items.hint: It is the first of three letters.

items.question: Which apostle wrote about the armour of God?
items.explanation: Paul describes the whole armour of God for spiritual battle.
items.hint: He wrote from prison.

items.question: What did Jesus say about the greatest among his followers?
items.answer: Whosoever shall be chief shall be servant of all
options: Whosoever shall be chief shall be servant of all
items.explanation: True greatness is found in serving others.
items.hint: It was said to the disciples who argued about status.

items.question: Which fruit is listed first in the fruit of the Spirit?
items.explanation: Love is named first in Paul's list.
items.hint: The list also includes joy and peace.

items.question: Which Christian virtue does Paul say is greater than faith and hope?
items.explanation: Paul says that love is the greatest of these three.
items.hint: The passage is often read at weddings.

items.question: Who was the apostle that the church replaced Judas with?
items.explanation: The apostles cast lots, and Matthias was chosen.
items.hint: He was with the disciples from the baptism of John.

items.question: Which apostle preached on the day of Pentecost and quoted the prophet Joel?
items.explanation: Peter explained that the Spirit had been poured out as Joel foretold.
items.hint: He stood up with the eleven.

items.question: Which early church leader was called 'the son of consolation'?
items.explanation: Barnabas sold a field and gave the money to the apostles.
items.hint: His name means son of encouragement.

items.question: Which apostle is nicknamed Doubting?
items.explanation: Thomas did not believe until he saw Jesus' wounds.
items.hint: He is also called Didymus.

items.question: Which disciple asked to see the Father?
items.explanation: Jesus answered that seeing him was seeing the Father.
items.hint: He was from Bethsaida.

items.question: Who was the disciple with no guile in whom Jesus found honesty?
items.explanation: Jesus praised him before he came to Jesus.
items.hint: He was from Cana.

items.question: What was the name of the Roman governor who condemned Jesus?
items.explanation: Pilate gave the order for Jesus to be crucified.
items.hint: He washed his hands.

items.question: Which king ruled Galilee when John the Baptist was beheaded?
items.explanation: Herod had John beheaded at the request of Herodias' daughter.
items.hint: He was son of Herod the Great.

items.question: What was the name of the high priest who sent Jesus to Pilate?
items.explanation: Caiaphas had earlier said it was better for one man to die.
items.hint: He was high priest that year.

items.question: What was the name of the Pharisee who taught Paul at Jerusalem?
items.explanation: Paul studied under Gamaliel.
items.hint: He advised caution about the apostles.

items.question: Who was the Ephesian silversmith who stirred up a riot against Paul?
items.explanation: Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis and feared losing business.
items.hint: The city was Ephesus.

items.question: Which Greek city did Paul visit where the people worshipped him as a god?
items.explanation: Paul healed a lame man, and the people called Paul and Barnabas gods.
items.hint: Barnabas was called Jupiter.

items.question: Which Athenian council member believed after Paul preached at the Areopagus?
items.explanation: Dionysius the Areopagite became a believer.
items.hint: Paul spoke about the unknown God.

items.question: Which city did Paul say he had fought with beasts at Ephesus?
items.explanation: Paul speaks of fighting with beasts at Ephesus, perhaps figuratively.
items.hint: It was a great city in Asia.

items.question: Who was the rich man who asked Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life?
items.explanation: He went away sad because he had great possessions.
items.hint: Jesus loved him.

items.question: Which Gospel records the story of the rich young ruler?
items.explanation: Mark records the encounter with the young man who had many possessions.
items.hint: This Gospel is the shortest.

items.question: Who was the high priest whose servant's ear Peter cut off?
items.explanation: Peter used a sword in the garden when Jesus was arrested.
items.hint: The servant was named Malchus.

items.question: Which Gospel tells of the angel who strengthened Jesus in Gethsemane?
items.explanation: An angel appeared from heaven to strengthen him.
items.hint: This Gospel is written to Theophilus.

items.question: What did Jesus say about children coming to him?
items.answer: Suffer the little children to come unto me
options: Bring the children to the temple
Suffer the little children to come unto me
items.explanation: Jesus welcomed the children and blessed them.
items.hint: The disciples had tried to stop the parents.

items.question: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do when they prayed?
items.explanation: Jesus taught them to pray with the words of the Lord's prayer.
items.hint: It begins 'Our Father which art in heaven'.

items.question: What did the Samaritan woman ask Jesus to give her?
items.explanation: Jesus offered living water to the woman at the well.
items.hint: The conversation took place at Jacob's well.

items.question: Which disciple was known as the one whom Jesus loved?
items.explanation: This disciple leaned on Jesus' breast at the supper.
items.hint: He wrote the fourth Gospel.

items.question: Who was the disciple who went with Peter to the high priest's courtyard?
items.explanation: This disciple was known to the high priest and got Peter in.
items.hint: He is the author of the fourth Gospel.

items.question: Which Jewish sect did not believe in the resurrection?
items.explanation: The Sadducees asked Jesus a question about the resurrection.
items.hint: They were associated with the temple.

items.question: Which feast did Jesus celebrate with his disciples when he instituted the Lord's Supper?
items.explanation: Jesus ate the Passover with his disciples before his death.
items.hint: It was the night he was betrayed.

items.question: Which Gospel records Jesus' words, 'I am the bread of life'?
items.explanation: Jesus described himself as the bread that comes down from heaven.
items.hint: This statement comes in the sixth chapter.

items.question: Who was the father of James and John, the sons of Zebedee?
items.explanation: The brothers were mending their nets with their father.
items.hint: The family were fishermen.

items.question: Who was the Herodian king who killed James the brother of John?
items.explanation: Herod put James to death with the sword.
items.hint: He was the grandson of Herod the Great.

items.question: Who was the apostle who was sent to preach to the Gentiles along with Paul?
items.explanation: Paul and Barnabas declared that they would turn to the Gentiles.
items.hint: They were sent from Antioch.

items.question: Which apostle is said to have been crucified upside down according to tradition?
items.explanation: Jesus foretold that Peter would be led where he did not want to go.
items.hint: Tradition says he was crucified in Rome.

items.question: In what city were believers first called Christians?
items.explanation: The disciples were first called Christians in this city.
items.hint: It is in Syria.

items.question: Who wrote the letter that says 'faith without works is dead'?
items.explanation: James teaches that faith must show itself in action.
items.hint: He was the brother of Jesus.

items.question: Who was the apostle who wrote 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ' in his first letter?
items.explanation: Peter opens his letter with praise for the living hope in Jesus.
items.hint: He was once a fisherman.

items.question: Which book in the New Testament is a letter written to Hebrews?
items.explanation: The author argues that Jesus is better than the old covenant.
items.hint: The author is not named.

items.question: Which letter speaks about the armour of faith, hope and love?
items.explanation: Paul writes about putting on the breastplate of faith and love.
items.hint: It is one of Paul's earliest letters.

items.question: Who was the apostle that wrote the letter from prison to Philippi?
items.explanation: Paul writes joyfully while in prison.
items.hint: Epaphroditus carried the gift.

items.question: Which letter is known for the words 'the fruit of the Spirit'?
items.explanation: Paul lists love, joy, peace and other virtues.
items.hint: It warns against returning to the law.

items.question: Which Gospel begins with a genealogy from Abraham to Jesus?
items.explanation: Matthew traces Jesus' ancestry from Abraham.
items.hint: It is the first book of the New Testament.

items.question: Which Gospel begins with a genealogy from Adam to Jesus?
items.explanation: Luke traces Jesus' ancestry back to Adam and God.
items.hint: It is the longest Gospel.

items.question: Who was the first deacon chosen by the twelve apostles?
items.explanation: Stephen was full of faith and the Holy Ghost.
items.hint: He was stoned to death.

items.question: Which person did Peter ask to cast a net on the other side of the boat?
items.explanation: The disciples caught a great catch of fish at Jesus' word.
items.hint: This happened after the resurrection.

items.question: What did the disciples catch when Jesus told them to cast the net on the right side?
items.explanation: The net was full of great fishes.
items.hint: The number is recorded in the Gospel.

items.question: How many fish were in the net that the disciples caught in John 21?
items.explanation: John records the exact number.
items.hint: The net did not break.

items.question: Which Greek word for 'love' describes God's unconditional love in John 3:16?
items.explanation: John uses the word agape for God's love for the world.
items.hint: It is the most common word for love in the New Testament.

items.question: Which Greek word did Jesus use for 'It is finished' on the cross?
items.explanation: The word means 'it is completed'.
items.hint: It is a word used for paying a debt.

items.question: Which church in Revelation was told it had a name that it lived but was dead?
items.explanation: Jesus said the church at Sardis had a reputation for life but was dead.
items.hint: It is one of the seven churches.

items.question: Which church in Revelation was described as lukewarm?
items.explanation: Jesus said he would spue the lukewarm church out of his mouth.
items.hint: Its people were rich but needed true riches.

items.question: What is the name of the island where John received the revelation?
items.explanation: John was on the island because of the word of God.
items.hint: It is in the Aegean Sea.

items.question: What was the name of the Roman centurion whose vision led to the Gentile mission in Acts 10?
items.explanation: Cornelius saw a vision and sent for Peter.
items.hint: He was stationed at Caesarea.

items.question: What was the name of the town where Paul was born?
items.explanation: Paul was from Tarsus in Cilicia.
items.hint: It was a university city.

items.question: Which city did Jonah first refuse to go to?
items.explanation: God sent Jonah to preach against the great city of Nineveh.
items.hint: It was the capital of Assyria.

items.question: Who was the king of Tyre who sent cedar for Solomon's temple?
items.explanation: Hiram sent his servants to Solomon to help build the house of God.
items.hint: Hiram was a friend of David.

items.question: In which valley did David fight Goliath?
items.explanation: The Philistines and Israelites camped on opposite hills of this valley.
items.hint: Its name appears in the first verses of the chapter.

items.question: How tall was Goliath, according to 1 Samuel?
items.explanation: The text gives his height as six cubits and a span.
items.hint: The measure is an ancient cubit.

items.question: How much did the head of Goliath's spear weigh?
items.explanation: His spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron.
items.hint: A shekel is a unit of weight.

items.question: Which tribe had no territory of its own, but received cities scattered among the others?
items.explanation: The Levites were given forty-eight cities among the tribes.
items.hint: They served as priests and ministers.

items.question: How many years did Israel serve Eglon, the king of Moab?
items.explanation: The Israelites served Eglon for eighteen years before God raised up a deliverer.
items.hint: Ehud was the deliverer.

items.question: How many years did Jacob serve Laban for Rachel and Leah?
items.explanation: Jacob served fourteen years for his two wives and six years for the cattle.
items.hint: It was seven years for each daughter.

items.question: Which king of Judah reigned for fifty-five years?
items.explanation: Manasseh's reign was the longest of any king of Judah.
items.hint: He was the son of Hezekiah.

items.question: What was Abraham's name before God changed it?
items.explanation: God renamed him Abraham, the father of many nations.
items.hint: The new name means father of a multitude.

items.question: What was Sarah's name before God changed it?
items.explanation: God changed her name to Sarah.
items.hint: Her name began with the same letters.

items.question: What was Jacob's new name after wrestling with God?
items.explanation: God told Jacob that he had striven with God and men and would be called Israel.
items.hint: It is the name of his nation.

items.question: Who were the two sons born to Joseph in Egypt?
items.explanation: Joseph named his first son Manasseh and his second son Ephraim.
items.hint: Jacob later blessed both boys.

items.question: Who were the two Hebrew midwives who feared God?
items.explanation: They refused the king's command to kill the baby boys.
items.hint: Their names are recorded in Exodus.

items.question: On which mountain did Moses die, looking at the promised land?
items.explanation: God showed Moses the land from the top of Pisgah on Nebo.
items.hint: It is in Moab.

items.question: Which city's mountain saw the sun and moon stand still at Joshua's command?
items.explanation: Joshua asked the sun to stand still upon Gibeon.
items.hint: The battle was against the Amorites.

items.question: Who was the father of Barak?
items.explanation: Barak the son of Abinoam was called by Deborah to lead the army.
items.hint: Deborah was a prophetess.

items.question: How many years did David reign in Hebron over Judah?
items.explanation: David reigned in Hebron for seven and a half years before ruling all Israel.
items.hint: His reign in Jerusalem was longer.

items.question: How many years did David reign in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah?
items.explanation: The total of David's reign was forty years, including seven and a half years in Hebron.
items.hint: The Bible gives the total in this verse.

items.question: How many sons did Gideon have?
items.explanation: Gideon had many wives and seventy sons.
items.hint: One son was named Abimelech.

items.question: Which city was the setting of Paul's sermon on the Areopagus?
items.explanation: Paul spoke to the people of Athens about the unknown God.
items.hint: It was the centre of Greek learning.

items.question: What gifts did the wise men bring to Jesus?
items.explanation: The wise men offered their treasures and worshipped the child.
items.hint: Two of the gifts are fragrant.

items.question: Where did the wise men first see the star?
items.explanation: They said, 'We have seen his star in the east'.
items.hint: They came from the east.

items.question: How many days after the resurrection did Jesus appear to his disciples before his ascension?
items.explanation: He showed himself alive by many infallible proofs during forty days.
items.hint: The number forty appears often in the Bible.

items.question: What was the tribe of Paul?
items.explanation: Paul describes himself as circumcised the eighth day, of the tribe of Benjamin.
items.hint: Saul, the first king, came from this tribe.

items.question: What was Paul's occupation?
items.explanation: Paul worked with Aquila and Priscilla making tents.
items.hint: Tents were made from goat hair.

items.question: From which city was Lydia, the seller of purple?
items.explanation: She was a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira.
items.hint: The city was known for dyeing.

items.question: Which island was Titus left on to organise the churches?
items.explanation: Paul left Titus in Crete to set things in order.
items.hint: It is a large island south of Greece.

items.question: In which city was Timothy from?
items.explanation: Timothy lived at Lystra and was well reported of by the brethren.
items.hint: Paul visited this city on his travels.

items.question: Which Roman emperor was reigning when Jesus was born?
items.explanation: A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed.
items.hint: He was the first Roman emperor.

items.question: Who was the governor of Syria when Jesus was born?
items.explanation: The taxing was made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.
items.hint: The name is Quirinius in other sources.

items.question: Who was the high priest along with Caiaphas during the time of John the Baptist?
items.explanation: Luke names Annas and Caiaphas as high priests.
items.hint: He was Caiaphas's father-in-law.

items.question: How many baskets of broken pieces were left after feeding the five thousand?
items.explanation: The disciples gathered twelve baskets full of the leftover pieces.
items.hint: The number twelve is important in the Gospels.

items.question: Where did Jesus go to be baptised by John?
items.explanation: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptised.
items.hint: The river is in the south of Israel.

items.question: Which disciple outran Peter to the empty tomb?
items.explanation: The other disciple outran Peter and came to the sepulchre first.
items.hint: He was the disciple whom Jesus loved.

items.question: How many lepers were cleansed when Jesus healed ten?
items.explanation: Jesus asked, 'Were there not ten cleansed?' Only one returned to thank him.
items.hint: Only a Samaritan returned.

items.question: How many days and nights did Jesus fast in the wilderness?
items.explanation: After fasting, Jesus was tempted by the devil.
items.hint: The number matches Moses on Sinai.

items.question: What did the devil tell Jesus to turn into bread?
items.explanation: Jesus answered that man shall not live by bread alone.
items.hint: It happened in the wilderness.

items.question: Who said, 'Be it unto me according to thy word'?
items.explanation: Mary accepted God's word through the angel Gabriel.
items.hint: She was the mother of Jesus.

items.question: Who was the father of John the Baptist?
items.explanation: An angel told Zacharias that his wife Elisabeth would bear a son.
items.hint: He was a priest of the course of Abia.

items.question: What is the name of the angel who announced John the Baptist's birth?
items.explanation: Gabriel stood in the presence of God and brought the good news.
items.hint: He also announced the birth of Jesus.

items.question: What did the people of Babel try to build?
items.explanation: They wanted to make a name for themselves, and God confused their language.
items.hint: The city was built on the plain of Shinar.

items.question: Which city was destroyed by fire together with Sodom?
items.explanation: The Lord rained brimstone and fire from heaven on Sodom and Gomorrah.
items.hint: Zoar was spared at Lot's request.

items.question: Which plague struck the firstborn of Egypt?
items.explanation: At midnight the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt.
items.hint: The Israelites were spared because of the lamb's blood.

items.question: What did the Israelites put on their doorposts at the Passover?
items.explanation: The blood on the doorposts marked the houses where the Israelites lived.
items.hint: It was an animal sacrifice.

items.question: Which feast celebrates the deliverance from Egypt?
items.explanation: The Israelites ate the lamb in haste, for it is the Lord's passover.
items.hint: It is still kept by Jews today.

items.question: What food came in the evening in the wilderness of Sin?
items.explanation: Quails came up and covered the camp in the evening.
items.hint: Manna came in the morning.

items.question: What did the people make while Moses was on the mountain?
items.explanation: Aaron made a molten calf from their gold jewellery.
items.hint: Moses broke the tablets when he saw it.

items.question: How many days did Moses fast on Mount Sinai when he received the law?
items.explanation: Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights without bread or water.
items.hint: The number forty recurs in the story.

items.question: What did Moses name the altar after Israel's victory over Amalek?
items.explanation: Moses said, 'The LORD will have war with Amalek'.
items.hint: The name means 'the Lord is my banner'.

items.question: On which mountain did Aaron die?
items.explanation: Aaron died on Mount Hor, and Eleazar his son took his garments.
items.hint: The mountain is on the border of Edom.

items.question: What did God give the Israelites to cure snakebites in the wilderness?
items.explanation: Moses made a serpent of brass and whoever looked on it lived.
items.hint: Jesus later compared himself to it.

items.question: Who anointed Solomon as king?
items.explanation: Zadok took a horn of oil and anointed Solomon.
items.hint: Nathan and Benaiah were also involved.

items.question: Beside which brook did God hide Elijah?
items.explanation: God told Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan.
items.hint: Ravens fed him there.

items.question: What did the angels sing to the shepherds on the night of Jesus' birth?
items.answer: Glory to God in the highest
options: Glory to God in the highest
items.explanation: The heavenly host praised God for peace and goodwill.
items.hint: It was announced to shepherds in the fields.

items.question: Where did the shepherds find the baby Jesus?
items.explanation: The shepherds found the babe lying in a manger.
items.hint: There was no room in the inn.

items.question: What did Jesus do when he was twelve years old in the temple?
items.explanation: Jesus listened to the teachers and asked them questions.
items.hint: His parents searched for him three days.

items.question: Which town did Jesus say a prophet is not accepted in his own country?
items.explanation: Jesus said that no prophet is accepted in his own country.
items.hint: He had been raised in this town.

items.question: Who was the first person Jesus healed on a Sabbath in Capernaum?
items.answer: A man with an unclean spirit
options: A man with an unclean spirit
items.explanation: Jesus cast out an unclean spirit in the synagogue.
items.hint: The people were amazed by his authority.

items.question: Which house of Simon did Jesus heal the mother-in-law of?
items.explanation: Jesus took her by the hand and the fever left her.
items.hint: It was in Capernaum.

items.question: What did Jesus do with the little children who were brought to him?
items.explanation: Jesus took the children in his arms and blessed them.
items.hint: The disciples had tried to stop them.

items.question: Which garden was the place where Jesus was arrested?
items.explanation: Jesus took his disciples to pray before his arrest.
items.hint: It was across the Kidron valley.

items.question: Which Gospel tells the story of the Samaritan woman at the well?
items.explanation: Jesus asked the woman for a drink at Jacob's well.
items.hint: It is the fourth Gospel.

items.question: What did Jesus say to the thief on the cross?
items.answer: Today shalt thou be with me in paradise
options: Today shalt thou be with me in paradise
items.explanation: Jesus promised the penitent thief that he would be with him in paradise.
items.hint: The other thief mocked Jesus.

items.question: Which man helped Jesus carry his cross?
items.explanation: Simon was compelled to carry the cross.
items.hint: He was the father of Alexander and Rufus.

items.question: Which man was released instead of Jesus at the feast?
items.explanation: The crowd asked Pilate to release Barabbas.
items.hint: He was a robber and murderer.

items.question: Which of the apostles is said to have led the church at Antioch with Barnabas?
items.explanation: Prophets and teachers at Antioch included Barnabas, Simeon, Lucius and Manaen.
items.hint: It was the church that sent out Paul.

items.question: Who was the first Christian martyr to be killed by the Jewish council?
items.explanation: Stephen was stoned while he prayed for those who stoned him.
items.hint: Saul approved of his death.

items.question: On which feast did the Jews gather in Jerusalem when the Spirit fell on the disciples?
items.explanation: The day of Pentecost was fully come when they were all with one accord in one place.
items.hint: It was fifty days after the Passover.
